solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: London section starts to spy on Home Office

indicators.note: the starts of the next four words are wanted, their opening letters only

explanation.surface: An agent begins surveillance of the government department responsible for policing and immigration.
explanation.definitionFit: Soho is a district of central London's West End, known for nightlife, so it is one section of the city.

clue.text: Former rent blown at Parisian day school

parts.note: ex- as a prefix means former

indicators.note: blown about, the letters of rent are scattered into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A tenant recalls the old rent being squandered at a school in Paris.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blown' is the anagram signal: it reorders the letters of 'rent' only, and 'at' is taken as it stands.
explanation.definitionFit: In French an externat is a school for pupils who go home each night, unlike a boarding school.

clue.text: Half of Oxford crew promoted king and country

indicators.note: taking the first half of the word for the crew, two letters of four

parts.note: Isis is the Oxford University reserve rowing crew, named after the Thames at Oxford

indicators.note: in a down clue, promoted means raised, so the king's name is read upwards

parts.note: Lear is Shakespeare's king

explanation.surface: Half a university rowing team gets a royal upgrade, along with their nation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'promoted' reverses LEAR to RAEL in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Israel is a nation in the Middle East, so it is a country.

clue.text: Everybody rejected boss who fiddled — a cowboy

indicators.note: rejected means thrown back, so the word for everybody is turned round

parts.note: all means everybody
the Roman emperor Nero is said to have fiddled while Rome burned

explanation.surface: Everyone turned down the crooked manager, who was a cowboy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejected' turns ALL into LLA. 'fiddled' suggests fraud, but it is Nero's legendary fiddle.
explanation.definitionFit: Llanero is the Spanish word for a herdsman of the South American plains, a cowboy.

clue.text: Nothing to hide about English beauty? Au contraire

parts.note: sweet FA is slang for nothing at all

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the hiding word goes round the English letter

parts.note: to cache is to hide away

explanation.surface: An English beauty with nothing to conceal, or perhaps quite the opposite.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts E inside CACHE after its first C. 'Au contraire' turns 'beauty' into its opposite.
explanation.definitionFit: Faceache is British slang for a plain or miserable-looking person, the opposite of a beauty.

clue.text: Retreat over one side of toll bridge

indicators.note: over means turned over, so the word for a retreat is reversed

parts.note: a lair is an animal's retreat

indicators.note: one side of the word means one of its halves, here the first two letters

explanation.surface: The traveller turns back before paying at one end of a toll bridge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' turns LAIR into RIAL; 'one side of' takes the first half of 'toll'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Rialto is the famous old bridge across the Grand Canal in Venice.

clue.text: Terribly cruel fun I'm describing?

indicators.note: terribly signals that the letters of the next three words are badly arranged and must be reordered

explanation.surface: Someone describes their own cruel brand of fun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Terribly' rearranges CRUEL FUN I'M, and the whole clue describes the result: the fun is pitiless.
explanation.definitionFit: Cruel fun is pitiless, lacking any mercy, so the whole clue defines the word.

clue.text: Stop wife leaving by trick

indicators.note: leaving means going away, so the wife's letter departs from the word for stop

parts.note: whoa is a call to stop a horse
X is the multiplication sign read as by, as in 3 by 4

explanation.surface: Stop the wife from leaving through some trickery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaving' drops W from WHOA, giving HOA.
explanation.definitionFit: A hoax is a deception played on someone, a trick.

clue.text: Saving loan is VAT free

indicators.note: free means let loose, so the letters of the three words are set loose and rearranged

explanation.surface: An advertisement boasts that a loan carries no value added tax.
explanation.definitionFit: Salvation is rescue or deliverance from harm, the noun sense of saving as in the saving of souls.

clue.text: Take pot-luck going round western state capital

indicators.note: western means heading west, right to left as on a map, so the letters read backwards
going round means the words wrap around the wanted letters, so they lie concealed within

explanation.surface: A traveller takes a chance on a route round a western capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going round' makes 'Take pot-luck' wrap the letters; 'western' reads them right to left. 'western' looks like part of the definition but is the reversal signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Topeka is the seat of government of Kansas, a US state, so it is a state capital.

clue.text: Joint stained with age, reportedly ornamented in a particular way

indicators.note: reportedly means as heard, so what is spoken is the phrase for a discoloured joint

parts.note: a knee is a joint, and yellowed means stained with age

explanation.surface: An old joint, discoloured by the years, is said to have been decorated.
explanation.walkthrough: Said aloud, KNEE YELLOWED gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Niello is a black metallic inlay used to decorate silver, so a piece inlaid this way is ornamented in a particular manner.

clue.text: She caresses student with more affection outwardly

indicators.note: outwardly means on the outside, so the word for more affectionate goes round the student

parts.note: fonder means having more affection
L for learner, the student driver's plate

explanation.surface: A woman strokes a student, showing more affection on the outside than she feels.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outwardly' puts L inside FONDER.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who strokes lovingly is a fondler; 'she caresses' points to a person who does that.

clue.text: Flying — no fear! Very fond of going backwards and forwards in a boat

definitions.text: backwards and forwards in a boat

indicators.note: flying means in disorder, so the letters of no fear are rearranged

parts.note: to be daft about something is to be very fond of it

explanation.surface: A fearless sailor who loves boats goes flying about the deck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flying' is the anagram signal for 'no fear'; 'going' is a link word before the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Fore and aft describes the length of a vessel from bow to stern, so it is back and front aboard ship.

clue.text: Select frozen dessert that's not cold in the middle

indicators.note: not means without, so a letter is dropped from the dessert
the letter removed sits at the centre of the dessert's name

parts.note: a choc ice is a block of ice cream coated in chocolate
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on a tap

explanation.surface: Pick an ice cream that isn't cold at its centre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not' with 'in the middle' removes the central C of CHOCICE. A choc ice is a British chocolate-coated ice-cream bar.
explanation.definitionFit: Select used as an adjective means of fine quality, a synonym of choice.

clue.text: Artist regularly having blunder framing people

indicators.note: framing means surrounding like a frame, so the word for a blunder goes round the picked letters

parts.note: bish is ... slang for a mistake

indicators.note: regularly means taking every other letter of artist

explanation.surface: An artist keeps making mistakes in painting portraits of people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes the even letters of 'Artist', and 'framing' puts them inside a British slang word for a blunder.
explanation.definitionFit: The inhabitants of the United Kingdom form a nation, so the word names a people.

clue.text: Mushrooms served up almost killed northern ska band

indicators.note: in a down clue, served up means brought upwards, so the letters are read in reverse

parts.note: ceps are edible wild mushrooms

indicators.note: in a down clue, northern means heading north, up the grid, so these letters also read upwards
almost means not quite complete, so the word for killed loses its last letter

parts.note: slain means killed

explanation.surface: Mushrooms on the menu nearly finish off a band from the north.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' trims SLAIN to SLAI and 'northern' reverses it; 'served up' reverses CEPS. 'northern' looks like part of the definition, but the Specials came from Coventry, in the Midlands.
explanation.definitionFit: The Specials were a Coventry two-tone group that led the British ska revival around 1980.

clue.text: Right on to be opposed and discarded

parts.note: taken as its opposite: the opposite of right is left
taken as its opposite: the opposite of on is off

explanation.surface: A slogan of approval, 'right on', is something to oppose and throw away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be opposed' tells the solver to swap each of the first two words for its opposite.
explanation.definitionFit: To leave something off a list is to omit it, so the phrase means discarded.

clue.text: Plump for bringing up feeble or stern protection?

indicators.note: in a down clue, bringing up means raising, so the word for plump reads upwards

parts.note: fat means plump
frail means feeble

explanation.surface: A choice between being plump or feeble, raised by a stern parent?
explanation.walkthrough: 'bringing up' turns FAT into TAF. 'stern' looks like strict but means the back of a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: A taffrail is the rail around the afterdeck of a ship, guarding its rear.

clue.text: How to label square off the top-right of a chessboard? That's idiotic

parts.note: as means how, in the manner that

parts.words: label square off the top-right of a chessboard
parts.note: chessboard squares run a1 to h8; one step beyond the top-right square h8 would be called i9

explanation.surface: A puzzle about naming a square that doesn't exist, which is silly.
explanation.walkthrough: Squares are named by file letter a to h and rank 1 to 8, so the square diagonally past h8 would be i9, read as I NINE.
explanation.definitionFit: Asinine means foolish like an ass, a synonym of idiotic.

clue.text: Vacillation overturned European statute about fines

indicators.note: about means going round, so the reversed letters surround the fines
a statute overturned is turned upside down, so the letters are read backwards

parts.note: a law is a statute
F for fine, as in pencil grades, doubled for the plural

explanation.surface: Dithering over a European law reversed on penalties.
explanation.walkthrough: 'overturned' reverses the European letter and the statute together, before 'about' wraps them round the fines; F for fine is a pencil-grade abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Waffling is dithering, being unable to decide, so it is a kind of vacillation.

clue.text: Start of fight — unexpectedly close quarters

indicators.note: the start of the word fight is its first letter
unexpectedly suggests things not in their usual order, so the letters of close are rearranged

explanation.surface: A fight breaks out suddenly at close quarters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unexpectedly' turns CLOSE into OCSLE.
explanation.definitionFit: The forecastle at a ship's bow traditionally housed the sailors' living space, their quarters.

clue.text: Melodious gospel-inspired music about extremely niggling female

indicators.note: about means around, so the music word encloses the other letters

parts.note: soul music grew out of gospel

indicators.note: extremely means at the extremes, so the outer letters of niggling

explanation.surface: Tuneful gospel music surrounds a woman who nags at the edges.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extremely' gives the outer letters of 'niggling', and 'about' puts them and the female letter inside the music.
explanation.definitionFit: Songful means full of song, tuneful, which is what melodious means.

clue.text: Whines awfully having just been born

indicators.note: awfully means badly, so the letters of the word are rearranged

explanation.surface: A newborn baby cries terribly.
explanation.definitionFit: Newish means fairly recent; something just born is recent in that loose sense.

clue.text: Drawing out non-adult instruction

indicators.note: non- means without, so the adult letter is taken out of the word for instruction

parts.note: education is instruction
A is the old film certificate for adult viewing

explanation.surface: Teaching for children involves drawing things out of them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'non' removes A from EDUCATION.
explanation.definitionFit: Eduction is the act of educing, bringing out or extracting something, so it is a drawing out.

clue.text: Dispute about your past fit

indicators.note: about means turned round, so the word for a dispute is reversed

parts.note: a row is a quarrel
thy is the old, archaic form of your

explanation.surface: A quarrel over one's past suitability.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns ROW into WOR.
explanation.definitionFit: Fit in the sense of suitable or deserving is a synonym of worthy, as in fit for the job.

clue.text: Banger in accident — police finally involved

indicators.note: involved means included within, so the letter is placed inside the accident word

parts.note: a hap is a chance happening

indicators.note: finally means the last letter of police

explanation.surface: An old car is in a crash and the police eventually get involved.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finally' takes E from police; 'involved' puts it inside HAP. Banger is British slang for an old, battered car.
explanation.definitionFit: A heap is slang for a decrepit car, the same thing as a banger.

clue.text: US state left 1,000 boys around northern islands

parts.note: Fa is a rare abbreviation for Florida, listed in Chambers
K, for kilo, stands for a thousand

indicators.note: around means surrounding, so the boys go round the northern letter

parts.note: lads are boys

explanation.surface: An American state abandoned a thousand boys near some northern islands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' puts N inside LADS. 'northern' looks like part of the definition but is just N; the islands lie in the South Atlantic.
explanation.definitionFit: The Falklands are a British-governed archipelago in the South Atlantic, so the name denotes a group of islands.

clue.text: Eastern republic taking question on nationalists

indicators.note: in an across clue, on means placed after, so the question letter follows

parts.note: the IRA, the Irish Republican Army, were Irish nationalists

explanation.surface: A republic in the east takes questions about nationalists.
explanation.definitionFit: Iraq is a Middle Eastern state with a republican constitution.
